target_customer: Music fans who read annotated lyrics (free, ad supported), with artists, labels and advertisers as the paying side
problem: Lyrics sites gave plain text with no explanation of references, slang or samples. Genius let a crowd annotate every line, starting with rap.
business_model: Ad-supported community knowledge platform with sponsored content, later media and licensing revenue
product_category: Consumer web, crowdsourced lyric annotation, music media

founders.name: Tom Lehman
prior_employers: D.E. Shaw or Google (Wikipedia says the three founders worked at D.E. Shaw and Google without assigning each)
education: Yale University (met cofounders there as undergraduates, per Wikipedia)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder and CEO; stayed CEO after the 2021 acquisition per Music Business Worldwide.

founders.name: Ilan Zechory
prior_employers: D.E. Shaw or Google (Wikipedia, not assigned per person)
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A web annotation tool and community moderation; the work was content and community, not research grade engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Millions of crowd annotations and contributors built a content library, but the lyric text itself was not protected, and Google showed copied lyrics in search.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google displayed lyric text in search from about 2019, which Genius said cut its traffic, and its 2019 lawsuit was dismissed in 2020 and upheld on appeal in 2022; MediaLab bought it in 2021.

market_need_then: Fans wanted explanations of dense rap references, and the founder said lyrics were an undeveloped web market; the idea started when Mahbod Moghadam was asked to explain a Cam'ron lyric.

branding.name_origin: Began as Rap Exegesis, renamed Rap Genius in December 2009 because users struggled to spell exegesis; shortened to Genius in July 2014 as it expanded beyond rap.
branding.domain_note: Operated as rapgenius.com, moved to genius.com with the July 2014 rename; acquisition terms for the domain not found.

identity.visual_style: Annotation highlights on lyric text, wordmark led
identity.voice_and_tone: Irreverent hip-hop insider voice early, broader music knowledge voice later

branding.brand_signature: Annotated lyrics where highlighted lines open explanations

rebrands.why: Expanded beyond rap to all music and other topics

branding.community_and_virality: More than two million contributors per Music Business Worldwide; artists such as Eminem, Nas and Pharrell invested in the 2014 round per Wikipedia; a 2019 public dispute with Google over copied lyrics drew wide press.

brand_strength.rationale: A recognizable media brand with a large contributor community and artist engagement, and a rename that removed a spelling problem, though the late sale at about the amount raised limits the case for iconic.

pivots.to: General music knowledge and annotation of other subjects
pivots.why: Expansion beyond rap; Genius was the new name

outcome_analysis: Genius grew from an annotation site for rap lyrics into a large music media brand, raising about 79 million dollars through a 2012 Andreessen Horowitz round, a 40 million dollar round in 2014 and 15 million in 2018. It lost traffic when Google displayed lyrics in search, its suit failed, and MediaLab bought it for about 80 million dollars in 2021, roughly the capital raised, followed by layoffs.
